correctness.rationale: PASS: A common Poisson global reset yields a unique stationary law. The empty-interval Markov recurrence E_(n+1)-(2+r/(2D))E_n+E_(n-1)=-(r/(2D))q^n, with E_0=1 and vanishing tail, has a unique two-exponential bounded solution; it is symmetric under exchange of its characteristic root lambda and Bernoulli vacancy q, including the repeated root. Inclusion-exclusion gives u=(1-lambda)(1-q)/(1-lambda q), v=u^2(1-lambda q). The quadratic inverse roots have discriminant z[z(1+u)^2-4u], proving the exact feasible wedge 4u^3/(1+u)^2<=v<u^2 and two ordered physical preimages except the equality merger. The local generator identity on an occupied origin gives m=2D+r q. At fixed u the permitted q(lambda) and (1-lambda)^2/lambda are both strictly decreasing over 0<lambda<1-u, with product ranging from infinity to zero; hence (u,m) identifies parameters iff m>2D. Independent symbolic algebra checked density, pair and recurrence identities exactly. These establish infinite statements analytically rather than by numerical samples.
